intro.en: Arabs have many proverbs. Some come from before Islam and some from the time of Islam. Each proverb has a short story behind it, and people use the proverb when something similar happens. Here are the stories in short.
intro.ur: Arab ke paas bohat si amsaal (muhaware) hain. Kuch Islam se pehle ki hain aur kuch Islam ke daur ki. Har misaal ke peeche ek chhoti kahani hoti hai, aur jab koi aisi baat ho to log woh misaal bolte hain. Yahan kahaniyan mukhtasar di gayi hain.
intro.ar: لِلْعَرَبِ أَمْثالٌ كَثيرَةٌ، بَعْضُها مِنَ الجاهِلِيَّةِ وَبَعْضُها مِنَ الإِسْلامِ. وَلِكُلِّ مَثَلٍ قِصَّةٌ قَصيرَةٌ وَراءَهُ، وَيَقولُهُ النّاسُ حينَ يَحْدُثُ شَيْءٌ مُشابِهٌ. هُنا القِصَصُ مُخْتَصَرَةً.

dialogue.ar: لِلْعَرَبِ أَمْثالٌ كَثِيرَةٌ، بَعْضُها كانَ قَبْلَ الإِسْلامِ، وَبَعْضُها جاءَ في عُصُورِ الإِسْلامِ.
dialogue.tr: li-l-ʿarabi amthālun kathīra, baʿḍuhā kāna qabla l-islām, wa baʿḍuhā jāʾa fī ʿuṣūri l-islām
dialogue.en: The Arabs have many proverbs; some were before Islam and some came in the ages of Islam.
dialogue.ur: Arabon ki bohat si misalen hain; kuch Islam se pehle ki aur kuch Islam ke daur ki.

dialogue.ar: المَثَلُ (١): جَزاءُ سِنِمّار. أَرادَ النُّعْمانُ مَلِكُ الحِيرَةِ أَنْ يَبْنِيَ لِنَفْسِهِ قَصْراً عَظِيماً.
dialogue.tr: al-mathalu (1): jazāʾu Sinimmār. arāda n-nuʿmānu maliku l-ḥīrati an yabniya li-nafsihi qaṣran ʿaẓīman
dialogue.en: Proverb 1: The reward of Sinimmar. An-Nu'man, king of al-Hira, wanted to build himself a great palace.
dialogue.ur: Misaal 1: Sinimmar ka badla. Hira ke badshah Nu'man ne apne liye ek azeem mahal banwana chaha.

dialogue.ar: فَبَنى سِنِمّارُ القَصْرَ عَلى أَحْسَنِ صُورَةٍ، ثُمَّ انْتَظَرَ أَحْسَنَ الجَزاءِ مِنَ المَلِكِ.
dialogue.tr: fa-banā Sinimmāru l-qaṣra ʿalā aḥsani ṣūra, thumma ntaẓara aḥsana l-jazāʾi mina l-malik
dialogue.en: Sinimmar built the palace beautifully, then waited for the best reward from the king.
dialogue.ur: Sinimmar ne mahal bohat khoobsurat banaya, phir badshah se behtareen inaam ka intezar kiya.

dialogue.ar: لَكِنَّ النُّعْمانَ خافَ أَنْ يَبْنِيَ سِنِمّارُ قُصُوراً أُخْرى أَجْمَلَ مِنْ هذا القَصْرِ، فَأَمَرَ بِإِلْقائِهِ مِنْ سَطْحِ القَصْرِ، فَماتَ.
dialogue.tr: lākinna n-nuʿmāna khāfa an yabniya Sinimmāru quṣūran ukhrā ajmala min hādhā l-qaṣr, fa-amara bi-ilqāʾihi min saṭḥi l-qaṣr, fa-māt
dialogue.en: But An-Nu'man feared Sinimmar might build other, more beautiful palaces, so he ordered him thrown from the roof, and he died.
dialogue.ur: Lekin Nu'man darr gaya ke Sinimmar is se bhi khoobsurat mahal banayega, is liye usay chhat se phenkwa diya aur woh mar gaya.

dialogue.ar: فَصارَ يُضْرَبُ هذا المَثَلُ لِمَنْ يَرُدُّ عَلى الإِحْسانِ بِالإِساءَةِ.
dialogue.tr: fa-ṣāra yuḍrabu hādhā l-mathalu li-man yaruddu ʿalā l-iḥsāni bi-l-isāʾa
dialogue.en: So this proverb is said to one who answers kindness with harm.
dialogue.ur: Is liye yeh misaal us ke liye bolte hain jo bhalai ka jawab burai se de.

dialogue.ar: المَثَلُ (٢): رَجَعَ بِخُفَّيْ حُنَيْن. كانَ حُنَيْنٌ إِسْكافِيّاً يَسْكُنُ الحِيرَةَ، فَجاءَهُ أَعْرابِيٌّ لِيَشْتَرِيَ مِنْهُ خُفَّيْنِ، وَأَخَذَ يُساوِمُهُ حَتّى أَغْضَبَهُ.
dialogue.tr: al-mathalu (2): rajaʿa bi-khuffay Ḥunayn. kāna Ḥunaynun iskāfiyyan yaskunu l-ḥīrata, fa-jāʾahu aʿrābiyyun li-yashtariya minhu khuffayn, wa-akhadha yusāwimuhu ḥattā aghḍabah
dialogue.en: Proverb 2: He returned with Hunayn's two shoes. Hunayn was a cobbler living in al-Hira. A Bedouin came to buy shoes and bargained until he made him angry.
dialogue.ur: Misaal 2: Hunain ke juton ke saath laut aaya. Hunain Hira mein rehne wala mochi tha. Ek dehati juti kharidne aaya aur bhaw-taw karte karte usay ghussa dila diya.

dialogue.ar: فَأَرادَ حُنَيْنٌ أَنْ يَغِيظَهُ، فَلَمّا رَحَلَ الأَعْرابِيُّ أَخَذَ حُنَيْنٌ الخُفَّيْنِ، وَأَلْقى أَحَدَهُما في طَرِيقِ الأَعْرابِيِّ، وَأَلْقى الآخَرَ في مَكانٍ أَبْعَدَ قَلِيلاً.
dialogue.tr: fa-arāda Ḥunaynun an yaghīẓah, fa-lammā raḥala l-aʿrābiyyu akhadha Ḥunaynun l-khuffayn, wa-alqā aḥadahumā fī ṭarīqi l-aʿrābiyy, wa-alqā l-ākhara fī makānin abʿada qalīlan
dialogue.en: Hunayn wanted to anger him. When the Bedouin left, Hunayn took the shoes and threw one on the Bedouin's road and the other a bit farther on.
dialogue.ur: Hunain ne usay chirhana chaha. Dehati gaya to Hunain ne dono jute liye, ek dehati ke raste mein phenk diya aur doosra thori door.

dialogue.ar: فَلَمّا رَأى الأَعْرابِيُّ الخُفَّ الثّانِيَ نَدِمَ عَلى تَرْكِ الأَوَّلِ، وَرَجَعَ لِيَأْخُذَهُ وَتَرَكَ ناقَتَهُ، فَأَخَذَ حُنَيْنٌ الناقَةَ.
dialogue.tr: fa-lammā raʾā l-aʿrābiyyu l-khuffa th-thāniya nadima ʿalā tarki l-awwal, wa-rajaʿa li-yaʾkhudhahu wa-taraka nāqatah, fa-akhadha Ḥunaynun n-nāqa
dialogue.en: When the Bedouin saw the second shoe he regretted leaving the first, went back for it and left his camel; then Hunayn took the camel.
dialogue.ur: Dehati ne doosra jota dekha to pehla chhorne par pachhtaya, wapas gaya aur apni untni chhor gaya; Hunain ne untni le li.

dialogue.ar: فَلَمْ يَجِدْ ناقَتَهُ، فَحَمَلَ الخُفَّيْنِ إِلى بَلَدِهِ، فَصارَ يُضْرَبُ هذا المَثَلُ في الخَيْبَةِ وَالإِخْفاقِ.
dialogue.tr: fa-lam yajid nāqatah, fa-ḥamala l-khuffayni ilā baladih, fa-ṣāra yuḍrabu hādhā l-mathalu fī l-khaybati wa-l-ikhfāq
dialogue.en: He did not find his camel and carried the two shoes home; so the proverb is said for disappointment and failure.
dialogue.ur: Usay apni untni na mili, woh sirf do jute le kar ghar gaya; yeh misaal nakaami aur mayoosi ke liye bolte hain.

dialogue.ar: المَثَلُ (٣): مَواعِيدُ عُرْقُوب. كانَ عُرْقُوبٌ رَجُلاً يُخْلِفُ المَواعِيدَ، أَتاهُ أَخٌ لَهُ يَسْأَلُهُ فَقالَ لَهُ: إِذا أَطْلَعَتْ هذِهِ النَّخْلَةُ فَلَكَ طَلْعُها.
dialogue.tr: al-mathalu (3): mawāʿīdu ʿUrqūb. kāna ʿUrqūbun rajulan yukhlifu l-mawāʿīd, atāhu akhun lahu yasʾaluh, fa-qāla lahu: idhā aṭlaʿat hādhihi n-nakhlatu fa-laka ṭalʿuhā
dialogue.en: Proverb 3: The promises of Urqub. Urqub was a man who broke promises. His brother came asking him, and he said: when this palm tree flowers, its blossoms are yours.
dialogue.ur: Misaal 3: Urqub ke wade. Urqub wada tornay wala aadmi tha. Uska bhai kuch maangne aaya to bola: jab yeh khajoor phool de to uska phool tumhara.

dialogue.ar: فَلَمّا أَطْلَعَتْ قالَ: اتْرُكْها حَتّى تَصِيرَ زَهْواً، ثُمَّ حَتّى تَصِيرَ رُطَباً، ثُمَّ حَتّى تَصِيرَ تَمْراً. فَلَمّا أَثْمَرَتْ سارَ إِلَيْها عُرْقُوبٌ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَقَطَعَ ثَمَرَها، وَلَمْ يُعْطِ أَخاهُ شَيْئاً.
dialogue.tr: fa-lammā aṭlaʿat qāla: utrukhā ḥattā taṣīra zahwan, thumma ḥattā taṣīra ruṭaban, thumma ḥattā taṣīra tamran. fa-lammā athmarat sāra ilayhā ʿUrqūbun mina l-layli fa-qaṭaʿa thamarahā, wa-lam yuʿṭi akhāhu shayʾan
dialogue.en: When it flowered he said: leave it until it becomes unripe dates, then fresh dates, then dried dates. When it bore fruit, Urqub went to it by night, cut its fruit and gave his brother nothing.
dialogue.ur: Jab phool diya to bola: ise chhor do ke kachchi khajoor ban jaye, phir taza, phir pakki. Jab phal aaya to Urqub raat ko gaya, phal kaat liya aur bhai ko kuch na diya.

dialogue.ar: فَصارَ يُضْرَبُ هذا المَثَلُ في خُلْفِ المِيعادِ.
dialogue.tr: fa-ṣāra yuḍrabu hādhā l-mathalu fī khulfi l-mīʿād
dialogue.en: So this proverb is said about breaking a promise.
dialogue.ur: Yeh misaal wada khilafi ke liye bolte hain.

dialogue.ar: المَثَلُ (٤): الصَّيْفَ ضَيَّعْتِ اللَّبَنَ. تَزَوَّجَتِ امْرَأَةٌ رَجُلاً غَنِيّاً، لَكِنَّهُ كانَ شَحِيحاً، قَدْ تَقَدَّمَتْ بِهِ السِّنُّ، فَاخْتَلَفا فَطَلَبَتِ الطَّلاقَ فَطَلَّقَها.
dialogue.tr: al-mathalu (4): aṣ-ṣayfa ḍayyaʿti l-laban. tazawwajat imraʾatun rajulan ghaniyyan, lākinnahu kāna shaḥīḥan, qad taqaddamat bihi s-sinn, fa-khtalafā fa-ṭalabati ṭ-ṭalāqa fa-ṭallaqahā
dialogue.en: Proverb 4: In summer you lost the milk. A woman married a rich but stingy, elderly man; they disagreed, she asked for divorce and he divorced her.
dialogue.ur: Misaal 4: Garmi mein tum ne doodh zaya kiya. Ek aurat ne ameer magar kanjoos buzurg se shaadi ki; ikhtilaf hua, usne talaq maangi aur usne talaq de di.

dialogue.ar: وَكانَ ذلِكَ زَمَنَ الشِّتاءِ، الَّذِي يَكْثُرُ فِيهِ المَرْعى وَيَكْثُرُ فِيهِ اللَّبَنُ. فَلَمّا جاءَ الصَّيْفُ احْتاجَتْ إِلى اللَّبَنِ، فَبَعَثَتْ إِلَيْهِ تَرْجُوهُ بَعْضاً مِنْهُ، فَرَفَضَ قائِلاً: «الصَّيْفَ ضَيَّعْتِ اللَّبَنَ».
dialogue.tr: wa-kāna dhālika zamana sh-shitāʾ, alladhī yakthuru fīhi l-marʿā wa-yakthuru fīhi l-laban. fa-lammā jāʾa ṣ-ṣayfu iḥtājat ilā l-laban, fa-baʿathat ilayhi tarjūhu baʿḍan minh, fa-rafaḍa qāʾilan: aṣ-ṣayfa ḍayyaʿti l-laban
dialogue.en: That was in winter, when pasture and milk are plentiful. When summer came she needed milk, sent asking him for some, and he refused, saying: in summer you lost the milk.
dialogue.ur: Yeh sardiyon ka waqt tha jab charagah aur doodh bohat hota hai. Garmi aayi to usay doodh ki zaroorat hui, usne maanga, us ne inkar kiya aur kaha: garmi mein tum ne doodh zaya kiya.

dialogue.ar: فَصارَ المَثَلُ يُضْرَبُ لِمَنْ يُطْلَبُ الشَّيْءَ في غَيْرِ وَقْتِهِ.
dialogue.tr: fa-ṣāra l-mathalu yuḍrabu li-man yuṭlabu sh-shayʾu fī ghayri waqtih
dialogue.en: So the proverb is said to one who asks for something at the wrong time.
dialogue.ur: Yeh misaal us ke liye hai jo cheez ghalat waqt par maange.

dialogue.ar: المَثَلُ (٥): عَلى أَهْلِها جَنَتْ بَراقِشُ. كانَ لِقَوْمٍ كَلْبَةٌ اسْمُها بَراقِشُ. وَفي إِحْدى اللَّيالي أَقْبَلَ أَعْداءُ أُولئِكَ القَوْمِ في الظَّلامِ يَبْحَثُونَ عَنْ مَكانِهِمْ، فَلَمْ يَجِدُوهُمْ.
dialogue.tr: al-mathalu (5): ʿalā ahlihā janat Barāqish. kāna li-qawmin kalbatun ismuhā Barāqish. wa-fī iḥdā l-layālī aqbala aʿdāʾu ulāʾika l-qawmi fī ẓ-ẓalāmi yabḥathūna ʿan makānihim, fa-lam yajidūhum
dialogue.en: Proverb 5: Baraqish harmed her own people. A people had a dog named Baraqish. One night their enemies came in the dark looking for their place and did not find them.
dialogue.ur: Misaal 5: Baraqish apne hi logon par jurm kar baithi. Ek qaum ki kutiya thi, naam Baraqish. Ek raat dushman andhere mein un ki jagah dhoondte aaye, magar na paya.

dialogue.ar: فَيَئِسُوا وَفَكَّرُوا بِالعَوْدَةِ، لَكِنَّ تِلْكَ الكَلْبَةَ نَبَّهَتْهُمْ بِنُباحِها إِلى مَكانِ قَوْمِها، فَهاجَمُوهُمْ، وَقَضَوْا عَلَيْهِمْ.
dialogue.tr: fa-yaʾisū wa-fakkarū bi-l-ʿawda, lākinna tilka l-kalbata nabbahathum bi-nubāḥihā ilā makāni qawmihā, fa-hājamūhum, wa-qaḍaw ʿalayhim
dialogue.en: They lost hope and thought of going back, but the dog alerted them by barking to her people's place, so they attacked and destroyed them.
dialogue.ur: Woh mayoos ho kar lautne lage, magar kutiya ne bhonk kar unhen apni qaum ka thikana bata diya; unhon ne hamla kar ke unhen khatam kar diya.

dialogue.ar: فَصارَ يُضْرَبُ هذا المَثَلُ لِمَنْ يَجْلِبُ الشُّؤْمَ عَلى نَفْسِهِ وَأَهْلِهِ.
dialogue.tr: fa-ṣāra yuḍrabu hādhā l-mathalu li-man yajlibu sh-shuʾma ʿalā nafsihi wa-ahlih
dialogue.en: So this proverb is said to one who brings misfortune on himself and his family.
dialogue.ur: Yeh misaal us ke liye hai jo apne aur apne ghar walon par museebat le aaye.

dialogue.ar: المَثَلُ (٦): قَطَعَتْ جَهِيزَةُ قَوْلَ كُلِّ خَطِيبٍ. قَتَلَتْ قَبِيلَةٌ رَجُلاً مِنْ قَبِيلَةٍ أُخْرى، فَاجْتَمَعَ رِجالُ القَبِيلَتَيْنِ، وَتَكَلَّمُوا في الصُّلْحِ، وَمَنْعِ الثَّأْرِ.
dialogue.tr: al-mathalu (6): qaṭaʿat Jahīzatu qawla kulli khaṭīb. qatalat qabīlatun rajulan min qabīlatin ukhrā, fa-jtamaʿa rijālu l-qabīlatayn, wa-takallamū fī ṣ-ṣulḥi wa-manʿi th-thaʾr
dialogue.en: Proverb 6: Jahiza cut off every speaker's words. One tribe killed a man of another tribe; the men of both tribes met and spoke about peace and preventing revenge.
dialogue.ur: Misaal 6: Jahiza ne har khateeb ki baat kaat di. Ek qabile ne doosre qabile ka aadmi qatl kar diya; dono qabilon ke log jama hue aur sulah aur badla rokne ki baat ki.

dialogue.ar: فَجاءَتِ امْرَأَةٌ يُقالُ لَها جَهِيزَةُ، فَقالَتْ: إِنَّ أَهْلَ المَقْتُولِ قَدْ قَبَضُوا عَلى القاتِلِ فَقَتَلُوهُ. عِنْدَئِذٍ سَكَتَ الخُطَباءُ، وَقالُوا: «قَطَعَتْ جَهِيزَةُ قَوْلَ كُلِّ خَطِيبٍ».
dialogue.tr: fa-jāʾat imraʾatun yuqālu lahā Jahīza, fa-qālat: inna ahla l-maqtūli qad qabaḍū ʿalā l-qātili fa-qatalūh. ʿindaʾidhin sakata l-khuṭabāʾ, wa-qālū: qaṭaʿat Jahīzatu qawla kulli khaṭīb
dialogue.en: A woman named Jahiza came and said: the victim's family seized the killer and killed him. Then the speakers fell silent and said: Jahiza cut off every speaker's words.
dialogue.ur: Jahiza naam ki aurat ne aa kar bataya ke maqtool ke ghar walon ne qaatil ko pakad kar maar diya. Tab khateeb chup ho gaye aur bole: Jahiza ne har khateeb ki baat kaat di.

dialogue.ar: فَصارَ يُضْرَبُ هذا المَثَلُ لِمَنْ يَقْطَعُ عَلى النّاسِ ما هُمْ فِيهِ بِمُفاجَأَةٍ يَأْتِي بِها.
dialogue.tr: fa-ṣāra yuḍrabu hādhā l-mathalu li-man yaqṭaʿu ʿalā n-nāsi mā hum fīhi bi-mufājaʾatin yaʾtī bihā
dialogue.en: So the proverb is said to one who interrupts people with a surprise he brings.
dialogue.ur: Yeh misaal us ke liye hai jo achanak koi khabar la kar logon ki baat kaat de.

dialogue.ar: المَثَلُ (٧): وَعِنْدَ جُهَيْنَةَ الخَبَرُ اليَقِينُ. خَرَجَ الحُصَيْنُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، وَمَعَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ جُهَيْنَةَ اسْمُهُ الأَخْنَسُ، اتَّفَقا عَلى السَّلْبِ وَالنَّهْبِ.
dialogue.tr: al-mathalu (7): wa-ʿinda Juhaynata l-khabaru l-yaqīn. kharaja l-Ḥuṣaynu bnu ʿAmrin, wa-maʿahu rajulun min Juhaynata ismuhu l-Akhnas, ittafaqā ʿalā s-salbi wa-n-nahb
dialogue.en: Proverb 7: With Juhayna is the sure news. Al-Husayn ibn Amr set out with a man of Juhayna called al-Akhnas; they agreed on robbery.
dialogue.ur: Misaal 7: Juhaina ke paas pakki khabar hai. Husain bin Amr nikla, uske saath Juhaina ka aadmi Akhnas tha; dono ne loot-mar par ittefaq kiya.

dialogue.ar: فَصارَ يُضْرَبُ لِمَعْرِفَةِ حَقِيقَةِ الأَمْرِ.
dialogue.tr: fa-ṣāra yuḍrabu li-maʿrifati ḥaqīqati l-amr
dialogue.en: So it is said to learn the truth of a matter.
dialogue.ur: Yeh misaal kisi baat ki asal haqeeqat jaanne ke liye bolte hain.

q.en: Which proverb is said to someone who repays kindness with harm?
q.ur: Kaun si misaal us ke liye bolte hain jo bhalai ka badla burai se de?
q.ar: أَيُّ مَثَلٍ يُقالُ لِمَنْ يُقابِلُ الإِحْسانَ بِالإِساءَةِ؟

q.en: Which proverb is said to someone who comes back disappointed and empty-handed?
q.ur: Kaun si misaal us ke liye hai jo nakaam aur khali haath lautay?
q.ar: أَيُّ مَثَلٍ يُقالُ لِمَنْ يَعودُ خائِبًا خالِيَ اليَدَيْنِ؟

q.en: «مَواعِيدُ عُرْقُوب» is said about a person who...
q.ur: «مَواعِيدُ عُرْقُوب» kis ke liye bolte hain?

options: brings bad luck to his people
knows the truth of a matter

q.en: «الصَّيْفَ ضَيَّعْتِ اللَّبَن» is said to someone who...
q.ur: «الصَّيْفَ ضَيَّعْتِ اللَّبَن» kis ke liye bolte hain?

options: asks for something at the wrong time

q.en: «عَلى أَهْلِها جَنَتْ بَراقِش» is said to someone who...
q.ur: «عَلى أَهْلِها جَنَتْ بَراقِش» kis ke liye bolte hain?

options: brings trouble on himself and his family

intro.en: Here you practise the proverbs: fill the blanks, match each situation with the right proverb, and learn singular and plural words (for example قِصَّة – قِصَص, a story and stories). You also practise writing sentences like those in the text.
intro.ur: Is sabaq mein hum misalon ki mashq karte hain: khali jagah bharna, har surat-e-haal ko sahi misaal se milana, aur wahid-jama seekhna (jaise قِصَّة – قِصَص, kahani aur kahaniyan). Matn jaise jumle likhne ki mashq bhi hai.
intro.ar: تَتَدَرَّبُ عَلى الأَمْثالِ: مَلْءُ الفَراغاتِ، وَمُطابَقَةُ كُلِّ مَوْقِفٍ بِالمَثَلِ المُناسِبِ، وَالمُفْرَدُ وَالجَمْعُ (مِثْلَ قِصَّة – قِصَص). وَتَتَدَرَّبُ أَيْضًا عَلى كِتابَةِ جُمَلٍ مِثْلِ جُمَلِ النَّصِّ.

q.en: A man promises again and again but never gives. Which proverb fits?
q.ur: Ek aadmi bar bar wada karta hai magar deta nahi. Kaun si misaal munasib hai?
q.ar: رَجُلٌ يَعِدُ مَرَّةً بَعْدَ مَرَّةٍ وَلا يُعْطي شَيْئًا. أَيُّ مَثَلٍ يُناسِبُهُ؟

intro.en: «إِلّا» means 'except'. The word after it is called المُسْتَثْنى. In a full positive sentence it takes the accusative: حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً (the students came except one student). In a negative sentence you may use either case: ما حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً or طالِبٌ. If the thing excepted from is not mentioned, the word follows the verb's role: لَمْ يَحْضُرْ إِلّا طالِبٌ.
intro.ur: «إِلّا» ka matlab hai 'siwaye'. Iske baad wale lafz ko المُسْتَثْنى kehte hain. Musbat mukammal jumle mein yeh mansoob aata hai: حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً (taalib-e-ilm aaye siwaye ek ke). Manfi jumle mein dono surtein theek hain: طالِباً ya طالِبٌ. Agar jis se istisna ho woh zikr na ho to lafz jumle mein apne kaam ke mutabiq aata hai: لَمْ يَحْضُرْ إِلّا طالِبٌ.
intro.ar: «إِلّا» أَداةُ اسْتِثْناءٍ. وَالكَلِمَةُ بَعْدَها تُسَمّى المُسْتَثْنى. في الجُمْلَةِ المُثْبَتَةِ التّامَّةِ يُنْصَبُ: حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً. وَفي الجُمْلَةِ المَنْفِيَّةِ يَجوزُ النَّصْبُ وَالإِتْباعُ: ما حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً أَوْ طالِبٌ. وَإِذا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ المُسْتَثْنى مِنْهُ أَخَذَتِ الكَلِمَةُ إِعْرابَها بِحَسَبِ مَوْقِعِها: لَمْ يَحْضُرْ إِلّا طالِبٌ.

vocab.ur: woh lafz jis ka istisna ho

q.en: In «حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً», what does «إِلّا» mean?
q.ur: «حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً» mein «إِلّا» ka matlab?
q.ar: ما وَظيفَةُ «إِلّا» في «حَضَرَ الطُّلّابُ إِلّا طالِباً»؟

options_ar: أَداةُ اسْتِثْناءٍ تُخْرِجُ ما بَعْدَها مِنَ الحُكْمِ

q.en: In «لا إِلهَ إِلّا اللهُ», the word after «إِلّا» is in the nominative because...
q.ur: «لا إِلهَ إِلّا اللهُ» mein «إِلّا» ke baad marfu kyun hai?
q.ar: في «لا إِلهَ إِلّا اللهُ» الكَلِمَةُ بَعْدَ «إِلّا» مَرْفوعَةٌ لِأَنَّ...

options: it is a negative sentence and the excepted word is a substitute
it is a full positive sentence
it comes after a question word only

q.en: The Arabic word for 'the exception' is...
q.ar: ما الكَلِمَةُ الَّتي تَدُلُّ عَلى «إِخْراجِ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الحُكْمِ»؟

intro.en: You listen to a text about proverbs and answer true/false and multiple-choice questions. Key ideas: proverbs give a clear picture of Arab life, and each proverb has a story. The second part is about the proverb «وَيْلٌ لِلشَّجِيِّ مِنَ الخَلِيِّ» and Aktham ibn Sayfi, who called his people to follow the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
intro.ur: Aap proverbs ke baare mein ek matn sunte hain aur sahi/ghalat aur chunao wale sawalat hal karte hain. Ahem baat: misalein Arab ki zindagi ki saaf tasveer deti hain aur har misaal ki ek kahani hoti hai. Doosra hissa «وَيْلٌ لِلشَّجِيِّ مِنَ الخَلِيِّ» aur Aktham bin Saifi ke baare mein hai jinhon ne apni qaum ko Nabi Muhammad ﷺ ki pairwi ki dawat di.
intro.ar: تَسْتَمِعُ إِلى نَصٍّ عَنِ الأَمْثالِ وَتُجيبُ عَنْ أَسْئِلَةِ الصَّوابِ وَالخَطَأِ وَالاِخْتِيارِ مِنْ مُتَعَدِّدٍ. الفِكْرَةُ الرَّئيسَةُ: الأَمْثالُ تُعْطي صورَةً واضِحَةً عَنْ حَياةِ العَرَبِ، وَلِكُلِّ مَثَلٍ قِصَّةٌ. وَالجُزْءُ الثّاني عَنِ المَثَلِ «وَيْلٌ لِلشَّجِيِّ مِنَ الخَلِيِّ» وَأَكْثَمَ بْنِ صَيْفِيٍّ الَّذي دَعا قَوْمَهُ إِلى اتِّباعِ النَّبِيِّ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.

options: has no sorrow in his heart

q.en: A short saying that has a story behind it is called...
q.ur: Mukhtasar qaul jis ke peeche kahani ho, kehlata hai...
q.ar: ما اسْمُ القَوْلِ المُوجَزِ الَّذي وَراءَهُ قِصَّةٌ؟

intro.en: Talk with a partner about proverbs: do all cultures have them, who writes them, and how do we benefit from them. Retell the six proverbs of the unit. Then discuss the meaning of six wise sayings, such as «لا وَرْدَةَ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَوْكٍ» (no rose without a thorn). Finally, summarise the opening text in your own words.
intro.ur: Apne saathi se misalon ke baare mein baat karein: kya har saqafat mein misalein hain, inhein kaun likhta hai, aur hum inse kaise faida uthate hain. Unit ki chhe misalon ki kahani sunayen. Phir chhe hikmat bhare jumlon ka matlab batayen, jaise «لا وَرْدَةَ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَوْكٍ» (kanton ke bina gulab nahin). Aakhir mein shuru ke matn ka khulasa apne alfaaz mein likhein.
intro.ar: تَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَ زَميلٍ عَنِ الأَمْثالِ: هَلْ لِكُلِّ الثَّقافاتِ أَمْثالٌ؟ مَنْ يَكْتُبُها؟ وَكَيْفَ نَسْتَفيدُ مِنْها؟ ثُمَّ تَرْوي الأَمْثالَ السِّتَّةَ في الوَحْدَةِ، وَتُناقِشُ مَعاني سِتِّ حِكَمٍ مِثْلِ «لا وَرْدَةَ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَوْكٍ»، وَأَخيرًا تُلَخِّصُ النَّصَّ الأَوَّلَ بِأُسْلوبِكَ.

vocab.ur: tum bote ho – tum katte ho

q.ur: «لا وَرْدَةَ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَوْكٍ» ka matlab...
q.ar: ما مَعْنى «لا وَرْدَةَ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَوْكٍ»؟

options_ar: كُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ يَصْحَبُها تَعَبٌ أَوْ صُعوبَةٌ
دَفْعُ الشَّرِّ قَبْلَ وُقوعِهِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ مُعالَجَتِهِ

options: as you sow, so you reap
necessity is the mother of invention

title.ur: Imla: «ما» ka milana aur alag likhna

intro.en: Rule 1: after a preposition, when «ما» is a question word it joins the preposition and loses its alif (مِمَّ، عَمَّ، فِيمَ، لِمَ، بِمَ، عَلامَ). When it is a relative word (that which), it stays separate: أَعْطِنِي مِمّا مَعَكَ. Rule 2: after إنَّ and its sisters and كُلّ, «ما» is written joined when it is just an addition (إنَّما، كَأَنَّما، كُلَّما) and separate when it means 'that which' (إنَّ ما بِعْتَهُ كَثِيرٌ).
intro.ur: Qaida 1: harf-e-jar ke baad agar «ما» sawaliya ho to preposition se mil jata hai aur alif girta hai (مِمَّ، عَمَّ، فِيمَ، لِمَ، بِمَ، عَلامَ); agar «ما» mausool ho (jo cheez) to alag likhte hain: أَعْطِنِي مِمّا مَعَكَ. Qaida 2: إنَّ aur uski behnon aur كُلّ ke baad agar «ما» sirf zaid hai to milate hain (إنَّما، كَأَنَّما، كُلَّما), aur agar matlab 'woh jo' ho to alag likhte hain (إنَّ ما بِعْتَهُ كَثِيرٌ).
intro.ar: القاعِدَةُ الأولى: بَعْدَ حَرْفِ الجَرِّ، إِذا كانَتْ «ما» اسْتِفْهامِيَّةً اتَّصَلَتْ بِهِ وَحُذِفَتْ أَلِفُها (مِمَّ، عَمَّ، فِيمَ، لِمَ، بِمَ، عَلامَ). وَإِذا كانَتْ بِمَعْنى «الَّذي» كُتِبَتْ مُنْفَصِلَةً: أَعْطِني مِمّا مَعَكَ. القاعِدَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: بَعْدَ إِنَّ وَأَخَواتِها وَكُلّ تُكْتَبُ «ما» مُتَّصِلَةً إِذا كانَتْ زائِدَةً (إِنَّما، كَأَنَّما، كُلَّما)، وَمُنْفَصِلَةً إِذا كانَتْ بِمَعْنى «الَّذي» (إِنَّ ما بِعْتَهُ كَثيرٌ).

q.en: «مِمَّ تَشْكُو؟» is a question. How is «مِمَّ» written?
q.ur: «مِمَّ تَشْكُو؟» sawal hai. «مِمَّ» kaise likha jata hai?

options: مِنْ + ما joined, as one word

q.en: Which sentence has «ما» as a relative word (separate)?
Which is written joined (just an addition)?
q.ur: Kaun sa milakar likha jata hai (sirf izafa)?
q.ar: أَيُّ جُمْلَةٍ كُتِبَتْ فيها «ما» مُتَّصِلَةً لِأَنَّها زائِدَةٌ؟

options: whenever you visit me, I honour you
options_ar: في كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ تَزورُني فيها أُكْرِمُكَ

intro.en: Arabic words are measured on a scale made of the letters ف ع ل (f-ʿ-l): the first root letter matches ف, the second ع, the third ل. So ضَرَبَ has the pattern فَعَلَ, شَرِبَ is فَعِلَ, and كَرُمَ is فَعُلَ. Extra letters stay as they are: سافَرَ is فاعَلَ, اِنْقَسَمَ is اِنْفَعَلَ, زَلْزَلَ is فَعْلَلَ. Dropped letters are dropped from the scale too: صُمْ is فُلْ.
intro.ur: Arabi alfaaz ko ف ع ل ke meezan par naapa jata hai: pehla asli harf ف, doosra ع, teesra ل. Is liye ضَرَبَ ka wazan فَعَلَ, شَرِبَ ka فَعِلَ aur كَرُمَ ka فَعُلَ hai. Zaid harf wese hi rehte hain: سافَرَ ka wazan فاعَلَ, اِنْقَسَمَ ka اِنْفَعَلَ, زَلْزَلَ ka فَعْلَلَ. Jo harf gir jaye woh meezan se bhi girta hai: صُمْ ka wazan فُلْ.
intro.ar: تُقاسُ الكَلِماتُ العَرَبِيَّةُ عَلى مِيزانٍ مِنَ الحُروفِ ف ع ل: الحَرْفُ الأَصْلِيُّ الأَوَّلُ يُقابِلُ الفاءَ، وَالثّاني العَيْنَ، وَالثّالِثُ اللّامَ. فَـ«ضَرَبَ» عَلى وَزْنِ فَعَلَ، وَ«شَرِبَ» عَلى فَعِلَ، وَ«كَرُمَ» عَلى فَعُلَ. وَالحُروفُ الزّائِدَةُ تَبْقى كَما هِيَ: «سافَرَ» فاعَلَ، «اِنْقَسَمَ» اِنْفَعَلَ، «زَلْزَلَ» فَعْلَلَ. وَالحُروفُ المَحْذوفَةُ تُحْذَفُ مِنَ المِيزانِ: «صُمْ» فُلْ.
